title: Cloth, Shirt, Sari, and Glasses
label: ch:bn-cloth-shirt-sari-glasses
canDo: I can name cloth, a shirt, a sari and glasses in Bengali, and say which word English borrowed directly and which is built on the same Persian word already met for 'eye'.

payoff.summary: The chapter closes on চশমা, 'glasses', built on Persian chashm, 'eye' — the very word চোখ's own lesson once named as its only cousin outside the family, here turned into 'eye-thing'. The reader names all four garments — kāpoṛ, jāmā, shāṛi, chôshmā — states that শাড়ি reached English as a direct modern loanword rather than through a shared ancient root, and reaches back to rescue the dative construction and ভালোবাসা, unrevisited since they were taught.
